item.title: 49ers owner Jed York’s prostitution suspension is over, so is he at NFL meeting in Manhattan?
item.description: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images 49ers owner Jed York’s prostitution suspension is over, so is he at NFL meeting in Manhattan? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Francisco 49ers have gotten off to a hot start to the 2026 NFL season, currently sitting at 6-0 following their recent home win over the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football. The team’s success has seemingly completely overshadowed the controversy surrounding owner Jed York, who was arrested this offseason for engaging in prostitution. York has been suspended for the first chunk of the NFL season, but that suspension recently reached its conclusion, opening the door for York to participate in his normal duties as a league owner. “#49ers owner Jed York, whose suspension has ended, is in attendance today here at the NFL meeting in Manhattan,” reported NFL insider Mike Garafolo of the NFL Network on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The NFL owners’ meeting offers a chance for the league’s top executives to review business strategy and make other key decisions for the future, and York will certainly be happy to be a part of it, even if he likely won’t be too eager to show his face in public for the foreseeable future. Still, his team’s success on the field has largely wiped away the stench of his scandal, as the 49ers sit as one of the league’s last remaining unbeaten teams, having found ways to win games despite injury struggles. Quarterback Brock Purdy is looking like an early frontrunner for the NFL MVP award at this early stage of the season, and the team’s defense has also not missed a beat despite the offseason departure of Robert Saleh. In any case, the 49ers will next hit the field on Sunday afternoon for a road game against the Atlanta Falcons. item.title: ‘We couldn’t have chose a better president twice’: Floyd Mayweather stands with Donald Trump
item.description: President Donald J. Trump speaks at a rally in the fieldhouse at Rockland Community College May 22, 2026. Monday, celebrity boxer Jake Paul attended a rally in Ohio supporting President Donald Trump, and just a couple of days later, another professional fighter joined the tour. Undefeated boxing legend Floyd Mayweather appeared in Bullhead City, Arizona, on Wednesday and, like Paul, endorsed President Trump before thousands. The boxing legend is just one of the many influential athletes who have backed the president during his tour. During Trump’s tenure as head of state, he has used sports as a platform and gained several major sports figures as supporters. He has also made his fair share of appearances at various sporting events, leaving no corner untouched, including boxing. Mayweather’s speech was brief, but he didn’t leave out his love for America, his Olympic experience, or his support for Donald Trump. “First, I want to say thank you to everyone that showed up,” Mayweather said . “America is the best country in the world. If I died and came back a million times, I would always choose America. It was great to represent this country in the 1996 Olympic Games, to go out there and represent the red, white, and blue.” “We couldn’t have chose a better president twice than Donald Trump. So it’s all about keeping this country strong, and it’s all about us sticking together and believing in one another. America’s the best country in the world, thank you.” The two have maintained an amicable relationship for over a decade, as Mayweather has praised Trump’s business savvy on many occasions. “We had Trump before; we didn’t appreciate him. But I think Trump is a great president; actually, he’s the best president, in my eyes, he’s the best president we’ve ever had. Great businessman, and that’s what it’s about,” Mayweather said on FOX Business’ Making Money with Charles Payne . Mayweather recently announced that he would be coming out of retirement, but his planned fights with Mike Tyson and Greek kickboxer Mike Zambidis have all either been canceled or postponed. Known to fans as “Money” Mayweather, the former boxing champ is currently battling the IRS and faces legal issues with an Audemars Piguet boutique in Las Vegas over a bounced $200,000 check. Needless to say, Wednesday’s Trump rally was Mayweather’s first public appearance in a while. item.title: Allegri: ‘Napoli avoid anxiety and haste, need patience in Champions League’
item.description: Allegri: ‘Napoli avoid anxiety and haste, need patience in Champions League’ Max Allegri explains his Napoli choices against Bodo/Glimt and urges his team to ‘never lose patience, because anxiety and haste lead to mistakes’ in the Champions League. It kicks off at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona at 20.00 UK time (21.00 CEST). You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game and Roma-Slovan Bratislava on the Liveblog. The Partenopei are in crisis after a dismal series of results, as they have lost both Champions League games to Arsenal and Villarreal. More damaging still is their Serie A form, fresh off a shocking 1-0 defeat to rock bottom Venezia on Saturday. Allegri eager to avoid Napoli anxiety FLORENCE, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 20: Massimiliano Allegri manager of SSC Napoli looks on during the Serie A match between ACF Fiorentina and SSC Napoli at Stadio Artemio Franchi on September 20, 2026 in Florence, Italy. item.title: Ravens' Week 6 loss to Browns is thanks in part to Derrick Henry's biggest flaw
item.description: Ravens' Week 6 loss to Browns is thanks in part to Derrick Henry's biggest flaw originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Baltimore Ravens are tied with the Cleveland Browns in the AFC North, with both teams sitting at 4-2 following the Ravens' Week 6 loss to Cleveland. Unfortunately for the Ravens, one of the main reasons why they lost was thanks to a problem that's been hurting Derrick Henry's game the last few seasons: fumbles. ESPN's Jamison Hensley highlighted how Henry's fumbling problem led to a Week 6 loss and is also much more than a simple once-in-a-while blunder. Henry's fumbling issues are a legitimate concern as his biggest flaw right now. Derrick Henry's biggest flaw with fumbles leads to Ravens' Week 6 loss "Running back Derrick Henry has now fumbled four times since the start of the 2025 season (23 games)," Hensley writes. "That's the second most in the NFL over that span, behind Buffalo running back James Cook III (five fumbles)." This fumbling issue hasn't gone away for Henry, and it might be the sole reason Baltimore lost to the Browns in Week 6. At the Ravens' own 35-yard line, Henry fumbled the ball, with the Browns picking it up, later scoring on their ensuing offensive drive. Henry has had some real fumbling issues with the Ravens, and this blunder against the Browns in Week 6 led to a loss. MORE : Cam Skattebo's lack of rushing attempts is a major cause for concern for Giants Of course, the Ravens were without Lamar Jackson and new center pickup Cam Jurgens. Add in that the defense gave up the go-ahead drive later in the game, and it's not all on Henry for their Week 6 loss. But Henry deserves plenty of the blame for the loss to the Browns. If he continues to fumble the ball semi-consistently, like he has the last two seasons, then the Ravens might be in a bit of trouble. They should be able to trust Henry to eat away at the game clock at the end of games. Instead, the Ravens now have to worry about a fumble whenever he gets the ball. The Buffalo Bills have a similar predicament with James Cook III, and it's a shame that these star running backs have such a glaring flaw. While Henry is a future Hall of Famer and can overcome this issue, it being such a real problem for the last two seasons should have the Ravens, at the very least, a little bit worried about his rushing ability going forward. It also brought up another reason it might be difficult to move Marte: He has a no-trade clause. Mark Polishuk wrote: "Only Ketel Marte knows if he’s a truly a trade candidate or not, as the ball is in the second baseman’s court when it comes to approving a deal. item.title: Oklahoma OC Ben Arbuckle’s ‘catastrophic’ John Mateer confession is damning indictment of backups
item.description: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Oklahoma OC Ben Arbuckle’s ‘catastrophic’ John Mateer confession is damning indictment of backups appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Oklahoma Sooners are 3-3 on the season after falling 21-13 to the No. 12 Kentucky Wildcats in Week 7. It’s been a roller coaster of a campaign, as that’s pretty much what you get with John Mateer at quarterback. While speculation has grown that it may be time for the Sooners to switch things up, offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle is seemingly humming a different tune. Arbuckle responded to a question asking why Oklahoma continues to play the redshirt senior. He claimed that he and the program fully believe that Mateer gives the Sooners their best chance to win on Saturdays, according to George Stoi III of Sooner Scoop, an affiliate of On3 Sports. The 31-year-old playcaller admitted that offensive mistakes have to be limited and took full blame for those errors. “We believe John Mateer gives us the best chance to win,” Arbuckle said… “We have to eliminate the catastrophic errors… Ultimately, it falls back on me.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Sooners’ backup quarterbacks are junior Whitt Newbauer and true freshman Bowe Bentley. Newbauer played at Mercer for one year before transferring to Oklahoma in 2025. However, he’s only played four games for the program. So, the backup situation simply lacks experience, as Mateer has 42 career games under his belt (24 with Washington State and 18 with Oklahoma). That lack of experience behind John Mateer is likely why the coaching staff is sticking with him. But at some point the up-and-down play may have to force their hand. Through six games this season, the 22-year-old has thrown for 1,308 yards, nine touchdowns, and seven interceptions while completing 65.1% of his pass attempts. We’ll see if the Oklahoma offense can cut down the big mistakes in Week 8. The Sooners are scheduled to take on the Mississippi State Bulldogs on the road. item.title: Liverpool legend labels Arsenal's Bukayo Saka a 'cheat' in heated rant
item.description: Arsenal's Bukayo Saka has been labeled a 'cheat' by ex-Liverpool star Graeme Souness -Credit:NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images Bukayo Saka is a "cheat" who "dives when he should be staying on his feet". That is the assessment of Liverpool legend Graeme Souness, who has accused the Arsenal forward of "simulation" and deceiving referees without actually being fouled. Souness unleashed the damning verdict during a fiery appearance on Piers Morgan's 'Football Uncensored,' arguing that Saka hits the turf too readily and that Arsenal players exert pressure on officials to sway their calls. The ex-Liverpool captain contended that the England international — currently the second-most fouled player in the Premier League this season with 21 fouls, behind Elliot Anderson's 23 — should remain upright rather than embellish contact, via The Mirror . Cristiano Ronaldo delivers brutal Portugal 'ultimatum' after Jorge Jesus 'broke his word' Brentford report strange and 'dangerous behavior' during Liverpool match to police Graeme Souness has slammed Bukayo Saka as a "cheat" -Credit:@SportsUncensord/X Saka previously drew scrutiny during a UEFA Champions League quarter-final match against Bayern Munich in 2024, when he went to ground after contact from Manuel Neuer, only for referee Glenn Nyberg to dismiss the appeals. The latest controversy erupted following Arsenal's 1-0 victory over Nottingham Forest on Sunday, with Saka again accused of diving — a charge that left Gunners supporter Morgan furious and prompted Souness to launch his attack. "Your man Saka dives all over the place. I don't want to hear about him. The minute he looks like losing possession, he's down," Souness said. "He simulates a foul. Anyone who simulates a foul in my book would be a cheat. "He dives when he should be staying on his feet. He's not alone. So Saka gets tackled, he screams as he's going down. The referee thinks there's nothing in that, but wait a minute, he's stayed down. And then worse than that, everyone in the immediate area - all Arsenal players - put their hands up and scream foul. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE "The referee at that point panics and blows his whistle when it wasn't a foul - his first instinct was the right one. But he blows a foul because he's thinking, wait a minute, something I'm not understanding here. "Simulation is a form of cheating, yes. But it's all over football today. If you asked 100 people what is it you dislike about the modern game, 50 percent would say simulation, another 50 percent would say VAR." Saka and Arsenal next take to the field when they head to Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday. They then face Everton in the Premier League on Saturday before making the trip to Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup three days later. It's a grueling stretch for the Gunners, who must navigate six additional fixtures in under three weeks before the next international break arrives.

item.title: Bruins’ Nikita Zadorov not at all pleased after being benched vs. Kings
item.description: Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images Bruins’ Nikita Zadorov not at all pleased after being benched vs. Kings appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Nikita Zadorov has led the National Hockey League in penalty minutes in each of the last two seasons — and his discipline cost the Boston Bruins defenseman a spot in the lineup over the weekend. Zadorov took three penalties in Friday night’s 4-2 victory over the Anaheim Ducks. Despite the win, head coach Marco Sturm made his most imposing blueliner a healthy scratch for Saturday’s 4-1 victory over the Los Angeles Kings. Speaking to Jim McBride of the Boston Globe on Monday, the 31-year-old said the decision left him feeling “disappointed” and “disgusted.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Still, the hulking Russian defended the physical, emotional style that has defined his NHL career. “Listen, we are Boston Bruins, and we play that brand of hockey, and I’m fitting this brand really well. And I believe it fits me pretty well, as well,” Zadorov said. “And I’ve been playing my whole life that way. I’m a big, physical D. I’m an emotional person on and off the ice, and I’m emotionally invested on and off the ice. So, when I go out there, I will die for any of my teammates and this logo that’s on my chest. “That’s what I play for, I play for the pride. So, when I go out there, I’ll leave everything on the ice.” Zadorov has already accumulated 29 penalty minutes in eight games this season, although he’s also contributed three assists and a plus-one rating. The former first-round pick has missed only three games as a Bruin since signing a six-year, $30 million contract with Boston in July 2024. Boston has a plus-20 goal differential with him on the ice during his tenure, underscoring the impact he can have when available. Despite the lineup shakeup, it’s been a terrific start in Beantown. The Bruins are 7-2-0 and in first place in the Atlantic Division, riding a five-game winning streak. Their last three victories have come on the road, with Boston defeating the San Jose Sharks, Ducks and Kings, in that order, during a sweep through California. The four-game road trip concludes in Dallas on Tuesday night against the 4-3-1 Stars. Zadorov could return to the lineup, although Sturm had not confirmed that decision. Puck drops at American Airlines Center just past 8 p.m. ET.

The NBA season is just hours away from getting started, with the Boston Celtics and Detroit Pistons slated to kick things off in the Motor City. The NBA is looking to build on the success of last year, when the playoffs drew enormous ratings as the New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs in the NBA Finals. Ahead of the new season, NBA Commissioner Adam Silver stopped by ESPN’s The Pat McAfee Show to give his outlook on the upcoming year. “I can’t remember a season that was so anticipated in terms of the level of competition across the league.. The East is loaded and we’ve got some great teams in the West,” he said, per Pat McAfee on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Silver also spoke on the NBA Cup, which has drawn mixed reviews from fans over its first three years. “The players love the competition and the fans have responded well to it,” he said. Silver had seen his public reception tank over the last couple of seasons due to factors like the NBA’s increasing partnerships with gambling companies, as well as criticisms about the league’s response to the tanking epidemic. However, he did win back some good grace with his harsh punishment of the Los Angeles Clippers for circumnavigating the salary cap in their signing of Kawhi Leonard, although some fans wanted more discipline for Leonard himself. Last year, the NBA Cup added a bit of legitimacy to itself when the team that won the Cup, the New York Knicks, also ended up winning the NBA title several months later. item.title: Carrick gives latest updates on several Man Utd injuries
item.description: Carrick gives latest updates on several Man Utd injuries Michael Carrick has confirmed Manchester United will be without several players for their Champions League clash with Como, with Lisandro Martinez, Kobbie Mainoo, Luke Shaw , Ayden Heaven and Marcus Rashford all unavailable. Martinez’s issue is not thought to be serious, but he has not travelled and remains a doubt for the weekend against Bournemouth after going off against Leeds. “It’s a bit of a mixed bag, we’ve got quite a few that are missing,” Carrick said. “Licha is not too bad but he’s not with us so we’ll have to see whether he’s ready for the weekend or not. “Kobbie, we’re probably looking at another ten days or so but not exact. “Luke, a little bit longer than that so a bit of injury and illness going through the camp but we’ll make the best of it for sure. “Ayden is ill. Marcus is still feeling a bit of a hip issue that we’re trying to overcome so hopefully that will be soon as well.” There was better news on Matthijs de Ligt, who is fit and available again after a lengthy spell on the sidelines. “It’s great to have him back,” Carrick said. “He’s had such a long journey of 11 months or so being out. He’s been patient, worked hard, so we’re delighted to have him back. “He’s fit, he’s ready, he’s been training for a number of weeks now so he’s in a really good place.” Carrick also provided an update on Benjamin Sesko, with United still waiting for a clearer picture on his recovery. “We’re hoping really soon that we’ll have a clear picture,” he said. “I’m not trying to delay it, hopefully next time we speak, maybe not tomorrow but by the end of the week, we’ll have something a little bit clearer. “There’s a bit of work going on at the moment so we’ll see what comes out of that.” Stay up to date with all the latest Manchester United news by joining our Man Utd WhatsApp channel .

For Bachmeier, life was good and only getting better — and then it all changed and there was nothing he could do about it. To quote Michael Corleone from the 1972 epic, “The Godfather,” “It’s not personal. It’s just business.” In the recruiting process, audibles are part of the game. Notre Dame did offer Bachmeier and whether he felt they used him as leverage to sign the kid they really wanted — five-star quarterback Deuce Knight from Lucedale, Mississippi — or something else, Bachmeier was left on the outside of their plans. It’s hard to blame Notre Dame. Knight was the complete package — he was big, 6-foot-5, 205 pounds, he ran the 40 in 4.5 seconds, had a 40-inch vertical, and brandished a rocket arm. Bachmeier was big too, 6-2 and 230 pounds with the ability to leap (ask the Utes) and throw (ask the Irish), but Notre Dame couldn’t help themselves. Stealing a five-star out of the South was irresistible. If it took a potential threat of landing Bachmeier to motivate Knight to commit — so be it. The second Knight was on board, Bachmeier and the other quarterback candidates became second fiddles. Whatever was said to them in their respective recruitment pitches no longer mattered. The Irish got their guy and that’s what mattered. “I think certain schools do it all the time. At the end of the day, roster spots are finite and schools have a level of urgency,” said college football recruiting guru Jeff Hansen of cougarsportsinsider.com. “You have a guy at the top of your board, and you are going to do whatever it takes to get him.” Instead of pursuing family dreams in South Bend, Bachmeier signed with Stanford. But after spring practice, the Cardinal fired his head coach, Troy Taylor. In a short period of time, the teenager’s topsy-turvy football life left him feeling wronged by Notre Dame and abandoned at Stanford. Seeking stability, honesty and an opportunity, he connected with Kalani Sitake at BYU where he became the first true freshman in program history to win the starting job . Marcus Freeman was Notre Dame’s head coach during Bachmeier’s recruitment, and even though it didn’t work out, both the Irish and the quarterback have been just fine without each other. Over the last two seasons, Bachmeier is 18-2 and Notre Dame is 16-3. On Saturday, playing opposite of his own gifted starter, CJ Carr, Freeman finally got to see Bachmeier up close and personal — and he saw more than he had hoped. Bachmeier threw a touchdown pass, he caught a touchdown pass, and he ran for two touchdowns in BYU’s win. “He confirmed exactly what I saw on film,” Freeman said after the game. “He is a competitive football player. He’s smart. He’s tough. You can hit him, but you won’t break him.” It is safe to say Notre Dame hurt Bachmeier’s feelings in the recruiting game, but they didn’t break him. Even when the Irish took a 24-21 lead in the fourth quarter on Saturday, Bachmeier responded with a 10-play, 55-yard drive and a 6-yard touchdown pass to Walker Lyons to bedazzle the nation’s top-rated defense and win the game. “I knew we were going to win this game,” Bachmeier told BYUtv’s postgame show, and when asked why he felt that way, he said, “Conviction. We have all the belief in everybody. We are tired of being disrespected and we were going to win this game. I was not going to lose to those guys.” Bachmeier not only conquered the Irish, but he also earned plenty of respect, including being honored as the Associated Press National Player of the Week. His Cougars jumped up six spots to No. 2 in the AP Top 25 for their highest regular-season ranking in program history. “On a personal level, kids are going to get upset by being used as leverage sometimes and they should. But it’s the nature of the recruiting game,” Hansen said. “Good for Bear to use it as fuel and not let it get to him.” In the wake of Saturday’s events, you could argue that Bachmeier got the last laugh in his dealings with Notre Dame, but that wouldn’t be accurate. He actually got the second laugh. The first was when Knight de-committed from the Irish at the last minute and signed with Auburn. Not all is lost on his grandfather’s dream for Bachmeier to play at Notre Dame either. Next season, the Cougars will stage a rematch with the Irish in South Bend. As late UCLA coaching legend John Wooden once said, “Things work out best for those that make the best out of the way things work out.” For Bachmeier, BYU and even Notre Dame, things are working out pretty well. item.title: Football Daily | Kulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?
item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White ” – Tim Russell. As an aside to the music makers and fitba’, in the late 60s at the old Highbury, we would be entertained at every first team match by the local constabulary brass band. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others). item.title: Uefa demands Fifa releases documents relating to World Cup sell-off scheme
item.description: European governing body gives two-week deadline Letter addresses other issues including Balogun affair Uefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan and other governance issues in its latest critique of football’s world governing body . A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months. These include the proposed sale of 20% of its commercial rights, the Folarin Balogun affair , the peace prize and relations with Donald Trump and the arrangements for next year’s Fifa presidential election. Uefa’s document also makes a number of allegations about potential conflicts of interests at Fifa, as well as repeating calls for a “genuinely independent” governance review. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
